subject: Architecture
title: Stonehenge: Sacred Circle of Mystery
description: A short lesson to help you apply Stonehenge: Sacred Circle of Mystery.

hook.text: Stonehenge's giant stones were dragged 150 miles across Britain 5,000 years ago. Nobody fully knows why.

buildup.text: The bluestones came from Wales. Some weigh 4 tons. They were transported without wheels or metal tools.

discovery.text: The stones align with the sunrise on the summer solstice — Stonehenge was a giant astronomical calendar.

twist.text: Recent DNA analysis shows the builders were replaced by a new population. Their descendants don't live there.

climax.text: Cremated remains of 150 people were buried at Stonehenge — it may have been a cemetery for the elite.

punchline.text: 5,000 years later, we still argue about why they built it.

quiz.question: Where did Stonehenge's bluestones originate?
options: France, shipped across the English Channel

details.summary: Stonehenge's stone circle, erected between 3000 and 2000 BCE, aligned precisely with the summer and winter solstice. Whether it served as an astronomical calculator, healing shrine, or ancestral monument remains debated.
details.whyItMatters: Stonehenge shows that sacred architecture encoded astronomical knowledge into stone. The alignment of massive stones with solar events reveals that ancient builders understood celestial cycles deeply enough to build permanent monuments oriented to.
takeaways: Precisely aligned with both summer and winter solstice positions
Built in stages over roughly 1,000 years (3000-2000 BCE)
Proves sacred building and astronomical knowledge were linked

faq.question: How is Stonehenge aligned with the solstice?
faq.answer: On the summer solstice, the sun rises directly over the Heel Stone when viewed from the center of the circle. On the winter solstice, the sun sets between the two tallest trilithons. This dual alignment indicates intentional solar orientation, not coincidence.

faq.question: Was Stonehenge a burial site?
faq.answer: Yes, in part. Cremated remains of over 150 individuals have been found at the site. Some were buried in the Aubrey Holes, circular pits within the monument's bank. However, burial was likely one of several functions — the site's solar alignment suggests astronomical and ceremonial roles as well.
